definition: Really Simple Licensing (RSL) is an open content licensing standard that allows web publishers to set terms for web crawlers gathering training data for generative AI use.
details: It was launched on September 10, 2025 and is managed by the nonprofit RSL Collective, co-founded by RSS co-creator Eckart Walther and former Ask.com CEO Doug Leeds. Participating companies at launch include Reddit, Yahoo, and Medium. Publishers can implement the RSL standard by adding licensing terms to their robots.txt files.

explainer.lead: Really Simple Licensing is an open content licensing standard letting web publishers set terms for crawlers gathering generative AI training data. It matters because it gives publishers a machine-readable way to state those terms.

tiers.eli5: Like a sign at the door saying what visitors may and may not take, written so web crawlers can read it.
tiers.practitioner: Publishers implement it by adding licensing terms to their robots.txt files. Pitfall: it standardizes how terms are declared, not whether crawlers honor them.
tiers.paperLevel: An open standard for expressing crawler licensing terms, added to robots.txt. Launched September 10, 2025 and managed by the nonprofit RSL Collective, co-founded by Eckart Walther and Doug Leeds.

explainer.example: A publisher adds RSL licensing terms to its robots.txt so crawlers can read the allowed training-data use.
